questions.question: Choice reveals preference was propounded by a) Marshall b) Hick c) Sweezy d) Samuelson (10x1=10 Marks )
questions.solution_html:
• Introduced by Paul Samuelson (1938) to explain consumer demand behavior empirically without
  • using subjective notions like utility or indifference curves. Consumer preferences are "revealed"
  • through observed choices in the market under given budget constraints.
  • Key Axioms
  • • Strong Ordering: The consumer selects a unique bundle of goods out of all affordable
  • bundles available within their budget constraint.
  • • Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (WARP): If bundle is chosen over bundle when both
  • are affordable ( is revealed preferred to ), then can never be chosen over at any other price
  • income situation where is also affordable.
  • Samuelson derived the Law of Demand directly from WARP using basic consistency
  • assumptions, proving that a negative income effect is not required to establish a downward
  • sloping demand curve for normal goods. Revealed preference theory states that the consumer's
  • product or service choice under different income and price levels provides information about
  • Page 15 of 2
  • their preferences. For example, if there were two combinations of goods (A and B) and if the
  • consumer chooses A (which is expensive) over B, then the consumer reveals their preference for
  • A over B. The theory is based on the premise that consumers are rational thinkers who compare
  • many options before making a decision. As a result, when a consumer selects one choice over
  • another, it must be the one they prefer. When a consumer's consumption pattern is determined by
  • observing the bundle of goods they choose over other alternatives, when all of them are within
  • the budget is known as revealed preference. A budget line is a diagram that depicts the
  • combination of products that a consumer can purchase at a certain income and price level. If
  • bundle a is revealed preferred over bundle b in budget set B, then the WARP says that bundle b
  • cannot be revealed preferred over bundle a in any budget set B'. This would be equally true had b
  • been located anywhere else on or below the blue line. The bundle c will not violate WARP even
  • if it is chosen in budget set B', because it is not on or below the blue line of affordable choices at
  • the time of the observed choice of a.

questions.final_answer: the time of the observed choice of a.

questions.question: Explain what is strong ordering
questions.solution_html:
• Introduced by Paul Samuelson (1938) to explain consumer demand behavior empirically without
  • using subjective notions like utility or indifference curves. Consumer preferences are "revealed"
  • through observed choices in the market under given budget constraints.
  • Key Axioms
  • • Strong Ordering: The consumer selects a unique bundle of goods out of all affordable
  • bundles available within their budget constraint.
  • • Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (WARP): If bundle is chosen over bundle when both
  • are affordable ( is revealed preferred to ), then can never be chosen over at any other price
  • income situation where is also affordable.
  • Samuelson derived the Law of Demand directly from WARP using basic consistency
  • assumptions, proving that a negative income effect is not required to establish a downward
  • sloping demand curve for normal goods. Revealed preference theory states that the consumer's
  • product or service choice under different income and price levels provides information about
  • Page 15 of 2
  • their preferences. For example, if there were two combinations of goods (A and B) and if the
  • consumer chooses A (which is expensive) over B, then the consumer reveals their preference for
  • A over B. The theory is based on the premise that consumers are rational thinkers who compare
  • many options before making a decision. As a result, when a consumer selects one choice over
  • another, it must be the one they prefer. When a consumer's consumption pattern is determined by
  • observing the bundle of goods they choose over other alternatives, when all of them are within
  • the budget is known as revealed preference. A budget line is a diagram that depicts the
  • combination of products that a consumer can purchase at a certain income and price level. If
  • bundle a is revealed preferred over bundle b in budget set B, then the WARP says that bundle b
